docs.contenu:
🎯 Objectives
- I can name the parts of my body.
- I can name my clothes.

🔍 Warm-up
Sing and touch: Head, shoulders, knees and toes, knees and toes! Touch each part when you sing. Now sing it faster!

📘 New words & structures
Body: head, face, eyes, nose, mouth, ears, hands, arms, legs, feet.
Clothes: dress, shirt, T-shirt, trousers, shoes, socks, hat, jacket.
Structures:
- I have two eyes and one nose.
- Touch your head! Clap your hands!
- I wear a blue T-shirt.
- Her dress is red. His shoes are black.

✏️ Practice examples
1. I have two ears, two eyes and one mouth.
2. Touch your nose! Touch your feet!
3. Today I wear a white shirt and black trousers.
4. Look at the baby! Her hat is pink.

🛠️ How to say it
To talk about your body and clothes:
1. Count body parts with I HAVE: I have two hands.
2. Say clothes with I WEAR: I wear a green T-shirt.
3. Add colours: My socks are white.

⭐ Remember
- Two eyes, two ears, two hands: add S at the end.
- One foot, but two FEET (not foots!).
- Wash your hands and your face every day.

🔗 Try at home
Play Simon says with your family: Simon says touch your head! Simon says clap your hands! Then look in your cupboard and say three clothes in English.

🎲 Fun corner
Robot game! One pupil is the robot. Give orders: Touch your head! Clap your hands! Stamp your feet! The robot moves. Mini-dialogue:
- What do you wear today?
- I wear a red T-shirt and blue trousers.
- Nice! I wear a white dress and pink shoes.
Extra challenge: sing the head and shoulders song three times, each time a little faster than before!

📋 Summary
We use I have to count body parts (I have two eyes, two ears, one nose, one mouth) and I wear to talk about clothes (I wear a blue T-shirt). Most body parts add S for the plural (eye→eyes, hand→hands), but foot is irregular: its plural is feet, not foots. Common clothes words are dress, shirt, T-shirt, trousers, shoes, socks, hat and jacket, and we add colours after: My socks are white. Remember to wash your hands and face every day, and to touch and name your body parts when you sing songs like Head, shoulders, knees and toes.
